title: Winning the 1937 citywide swing contest at St. Monica's
summary: He describes the lineup that won the contest against Joe Robichaux, Professor Victor and Henry Harden before 10,000 people.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Who were playing with you then?
Well I had Benny Allen on piano, I had Gaudet playing trumpet, Willie Humphrey playing clarinet.

The one you know, yeah. No, the young one. The one was here now, you know. Yeah, not his daddy. No, he was playing clarinet, Jerry Green was playing bass, and Raymond Carlis was playing drums. And we won the contest. Out of all those bands, well I came in with the swing, Professor Victor come in with the sweet music, and Henry Hardin, he come in with the best dressed band. And Salestand and Joe Rocio and them were, it was automatically mentioned. Well I had a band similar to, at that time, we was on the style of Lionel Hampton, when Charlie was the best dressed and all of them was with Benny Goodwin. That's our band. That's our band. Well I'm just trying to give you an idea. We were the best band. We were the best band. We were the best band. We were the best band. So that's it. Now who was Wes, you said he was down here with the band?
And Earl Bostick, he come down here to go to school.

Well he played saxophone too. But he left here and he went back with, was it Alvin Walters, he went back with, I can't think of them bands, went back to Oklahoma. See they're all from Oklahoma. And they had Porter, trumpet player, Bucket, and all that bunch, they was, and Killdeed they called him, all that bunch was with Joe Roachio. That's where his band comes. And this boy would play all that trumpet, used to be with Count, boy from, I can't think of his name, his daddy used to play with the Creole Serenade, used to play piano, you know with Dyer, what's his name? Dyer.
Is he any kind of Dwight Newman?

That's Dwight, little Dwight, Dwight's son. Oh you mean Joe? Joe Newman, yeah. Well that's the bunch who was playing with Victor and them that I won the contest against. And Wallace Davenport and all that bunch was with Victor so you know how much they had in the band. Oh yeah. We made 10,000 people stand up and listen.

And first, that was 1937. And you had 10,000 people there? 10,000 people. I won the swing contest up the city. Well the judges, George McDermott used to have a place, he died, he got killed in a place of establishment. And this Fourier, they call him Beansley, they used to have all that gambling, all that bunch. They were the judges back then, some of the judges, and the priests included, you know, back then. The priests in Beansley, that was a good combination. No, the priests had charge of the, you know, trying to raise money to help that school, you know, that St. Monica School. Well it was a city wide contest, and I won the contest.
Where did they put all the people? Was it in a big, a lot of them?

Yeah. It was all out in the yard and everything. It's a school, but the other place is still right back there. Yeah. I had some of the Thai classes, a lot of clippings, but about transforming, moving so much, you know what I mean? Yeah. I met you somewhere, where did I meet you?
